column1: # Known failures, reported and not enforced (docs/languages.md 12.1). The UniMorph rows are from the same
# sample as corpus.tsv (UniMorph eng 66e0e9e, CC BY-SA 3.0, by the UniMorph contributors); README.md, Known gaps.
# eas -> ea: ea (a Scots word for a river) is a two-letter stem ending in a vowel; -s after such a stem is not read, so has, was and his do not become ha, wa and hi
# red -> rede: rede (to advise) is archaic; -d after a two-letter stem is not read, because bed and wed would become be and we
# envied -> envie: envie is an obsolete spelling of envy (found); -ied is read as -y except for the -ie verbs the rules list, since Wiktionary also has trie and marrie
# shied -> shie: shie is an obsolete spelling of shy (found); as for envied
# stolen -> steale: steale is an obsolete spelling of steal; the rules give steal
# former -> fore: former is an adjective of its own; fore has no comparative in current English
